title: Systems Awareness
equation: Output Score = (Input Quality + Structure Quality + Feedback Speed) ÷ 3
hook: If the same problem keeps coming back every month, you don't have a task. You have a system.
statement: Everything is a system with inputs, outputs, and feedback.
explainer: Treat things like a to-do list and you fix the same thing forever. See the system and you can find the part that's actually broken and fix it once.
sop: Pick one problem that keeps coming back.
Write down every part involved and how they connect.
Score Input Quality, Structure Quality, and Feedback Speed 1 to 10.
Start with whichever score is lowest.
Check again in 30 days to see if the system changed, not just the symptom.
equation_example: Input Quality 7, Structure Quality 5, Feedback Speed 8. (7 + 5 + 8) ÷ 3 = 6.7 out of 10. Higher means the system runs well on its own. Lower means one weak part, here the structure, is dragging the rest down.
question: Pick one area you're still running as a to-do list and sketch it out as a system.
closing_statement: See the mechanism, not just the moving parts.
caption:
Principle Nº 101: Systems Awareness

If the same problem keeps coming back every month, you don't have a task. You have a system.

Everything is a system with inputs, outputs, and feedback.

Your turn: Pick one area you're still running as a to-do list and sketch it out as a system.
